dependencies.basis: INE Guinea-Bissau's own fuller technical note (a different edition of the same INHPC bulletin family already minted as `gw-ine-inhpc`) states directly: "O actual IHPC - (base 2014=100) é produzido e publicado em cada Estado Membro, de acordo com a metodologia desenvolvida por especialistas no domínio dos preços, no âmbito do grupo de trabalho da UEMOA e Observatório Económico e Estatístico da Africa Subsahariana (AFRISTAT)" [The current IHPC (base 2014=100) is produced and published in each Member State according to the methodology developed by price-domain specialists within the UEMOA working group and AFRISTAT]. A second, later edition (January 2025) corroborates: "metodologia comum, adotada em 1996 pelos oito países membros da União Económica e Monetária da África Ocidental (UEMOA)" [common methodology, adopted in 1996 by the eight UEMOA member states]. Guinea-Bissau uses the West African CFA franc and is a genuine UEMOA/BCEAO member (unlike most of this wave's countries), so this is a real, direct methodology dependency — not a mere support-mention. `afristat-ihpc-guide-2014` reused per the branch's node-id discipline (7th country citing it this session).

_dropped.why: MUNICIPAL-TIER LEAD, deliberately not pursued this round per Thomas's instruction to hold off on municipal for now. Guinea-Bissau's Constitution (Lei Constitucional nº1/96, directly verified via FAOLEX), Article 110 §1-2: "As autarquias locais têm património e finanças próprios. O regime das finanças locais, a estabelecer por lei, deverá visar a justa repartição dos recursos públicos pelo Estado e pelas autarquias locais" [Local authorities have their own patrimony and finances; the local finance regime must aim at a fair distribution of public resources between the State and local authorities]. Article 118 grants autarquias a share of direct-tax revenue. IMPORTANT: this fiscal-sharing guarantee applies ONLY to "autarquias locais" (municípios, secções autárquicas, juntas locais, per Art. 106) — a MUNICIPAL tier, not the 9 regiões. Art. 107 defines regiões as purely deconcentrated political-administrative divisions with centrally-appointed governors (Art. 108), i.e. NOT a decentralised fiscal tier at all. Art. 107 §2 defers regional organisation to a separate ordinary law, which could not be located online this round — genuine NOT FOUND for the provincial/regional tier specifically requested.
